newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia stocks continue rally, blue chips lead way.
newsitem.headline: Croatia stocks continue rally, blue chips lead way.

text.p: Croatian stocks, led by blue chips, continued to rally on Wednesday in lively trade, showcasing Zagrebacka Banka and food concern Podravka.
Traders predicted the bull run would continue until the end of the week. "I expect the prices to grow further in the next two days," Igor Kos of Taurus brokerage said.
Another trader linked recent gains to expectations of a good credit rating for Croatia. Three leading rating agencies are to announce their assessment by the end of the week.
"If the rating is positive, it could prompt a new wave of foreign investment into Croatia and then prices would go up again," Marko Nikolac of Metroholding brokerage said.
Of 13 active issues eight were up, four down and one flat. Volume was lower at 11,201 shares but turnover up at 8.8 million kuna.
Biggest gainer, fully-listed Zagrebacka Banka, jumped 245 kuna to 1,600 with 3,312 units sold. Its GDRs in London peaked at highest-ever $29.06 from Tuesday's close at $27.875.
Another blue chip, drug firm Pliva also gained 2 kuna to close at 490 on volume of 2,370 units. Its GDR's also rose to $18,875 from Tuesday's close at $17.63.
Podravka was the most active stock, gaining nine kuna to 264 on volume of 6,198 shares.
Chocolate maker Kras lost 15 kuna to close at 1,200, selling 243 shares.

While both traders cautioned the January growth was "slightly unrealistic", they said the blue chips and several other issues, including Podravka and Kras had solid "grounds for objective further growth".
Wednesday's biggest loser was hotelier Arenaturist, falling 20 kuna to close at 150 trading 340 units.
